full_judgment: 10. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellants, submits that the High Court Division committed error in dismissing the suit without adverting to the findings arrived at by the Court of appeal which decreed the suit on consideration of possession of the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs and as such, the impugned judgment should be set aside. He further submits that the High Court Division erred in law in applying the amended provision of section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act and in the instant case lease had been granted by the landlord by executing and registering a patta in the year 1925 and that execution of a lease deed, by the lessor as well as by the lessee was not mandatory before 1929. He then submits that the Court of appeal below decreed the suit by taking into consideration that Abdur Rahman was in possession of the suit land on the strength of the patta executed by the Nazir Ahmed and that as soon as the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act came into force, he became a rayiat under the Government and thus while making the Rule absolute, the High Court Division failed to consider the aforesaid finding of the appellate Court. He lastly submits that the High Court Division committed error in rejecting exhibit-3, the registered patta dated 18.07.1925 by the landlord treating the same as a lease deed under section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act and committed error in not considering that when the Bengal Tenancy Act was in operation, the landlord had authority to grant patta in respect of the suit land and a patta is always a document executed only by the landlord under the then circumstances.
